transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

For weeks I’ve had this nonstop drive to take on more at the hospital, like I can’t slow my mind or body down even when I know it’s too much. It’s just really starting to overwhelm me and I don't know how to stop it.
Have you ever had another time in your life when you felt this same kind of unusually high energy and racing mind for several days or longer, or is this the first episode like this?

No, this is definitely the first time I've ever experienced this kind of high energy or the crash afterwards. It all started about two months ago when I began juggling my first job, working night shifts, and studying for my CNA exam.

During this period, did you need much less sleep than usual and still feel energetic, or did the symptoms mainly happen when you were under stress from work and studying? Also, did anyone notice you were unusually talkative, impulsive, or overly confident?

Yeah, I was only getting three or four hours of sleep a night but still felt totally wired, which all started while I was super stressed with my night shifts and CNA exam prep. My parents and coworkers definitely noticed because they said I was talking a mile a minute, and I honestly felt so confident that I thought I understood patient care better than the actual nurses.

Even when work or exam stress was not happening, did you still feel unusually energetic and overly confident for at least several days in a row? Or did those symptoms only show up during the stressful periods?

Honestly, the stress from my new job, night shifts, and studying has been completely constant for the last two months, so I haven't really had a stress-free period to see if it would happen on its own. But that intense, high-energy phase lasted continuously for several weeks straight during that stressful time before I finally crashed.

During those several weeks, did your symptoms ever get so severe that you got into serious trouble at work or school, needed emergency help or hospitalization, or had experiences like hearing things others didn’t? Or was it mainly feeling revved up and overwhelmed without that level of loss of control?

Honestly, it got really bad and I completely lost control of things. I ended up getting written up at work for staying late and ignoring protocols, and I've missed several shifts and classes because of it. On top of that, during those late nights when I was alone, I kept hearing this calm male voice telling me I was "chosen to fix the system."

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a first episode of sustained elevated/expansive mood and increased energy lasting several weeks, with decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, grandiosity, occupational impairment, and psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations/congruent delusional theme). This is most consistent with a manic episode with psychotic symptoms. Although psychosocial stressors were present, the syndrome exceeded a simple stress reaction and included core manic and psychotic features.
